curriculum.lesson_evidence: A kitchen audit looks for evidence of hazards, then ranks what to fix first. Ready-to-eat food under raw meat, no soap at the sink, and a stew left out overnight are not equal. The overnight stew is discarded. The shelf order is changed before the next shop. Soap is replaced before the next wash. The audit records what you saw, not a general slogan.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A different kitchen: a dirty floor, a clean fridge with milk in the door that is still cold, and a sandwich made after handling raw eggs with unwashed hands. Which issue do you fix in the food itself, and why is the floor not first?

FEEDBACK
The sandwich is unsafe and should not be eaten; wash hands and remake it. A dirty floor matters for cleaning, but it is not in the food. Cold milk in the door is a lower priority if it is still cold.

WATCH FOR
Cleaning the visible floor first and serving the risky sandwich because the plate looks neat. Evidence of contamination beats appearance.
lesson.independent_task:

Audit this new scene in writing: thawed prawns on the top shelf above a custard, one shared towel for hands and the floor, and hot soup being cooled in a deep pot with the lid on. Give an order of actions and one revised cooling method.

Write a short reflection naming one observation, criterion or step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Seen: raw chicken uncovered above cut oranges; soap bottle empty; rice pot on the stove from yesterday. First: discard the rice. Second: move or discard anything the chicken dripped on, then rewash the area and store raw meat below. Third: refill soap before any washing. The order follows harm, not how easy the job looks.

TRY FIRST
A different kitchen: a dirty floor, a clean fridge with milk in the door that is still cold, and a sandwich made after handling raw eggs with unwashed hands. Which issue do you fix in the food itself, and why is the floor not first?

FEEDBACK
The sandwich is unsafe and should not be eaten; wash hands and remake it. A dirty floor matters for cleaning, but it is not in the food. Cold milk in the door is a lower priority if it is still cold.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen, measured or tested against criteria.
